description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Following the adoption of NIMP aiming to better align irrigation development with agriculture policy and accelerate development of modern and resilient irrigation systems, the government (i) transferred the NIA from the Office of the President to the Department of Agriculture, by issuing an executive order, to optimize the use of water resources and improve the state of food security in view of the significant effects of climate change and the COVID-19 pandemic; (ii) secured ₱42.1 billion in the 2021 General Appropriations Act (GAA) and 2022 GAA allocated to priority investment projects of NIMP; and (iii) mainstreamed the preparation of gender and development plans.

Following the approval of the Administrative Order on the institutionalization of the Agriculture Dialogue and Information Network Groups (ADING) Program as DA's integrity management and advocacy program, the government amended the Administrative Order to ensure (i) appropriate budget allocations for implementation of the ADING program at the regional and local levels, including meetings, consultations, and monitoring and feedback activities; and (ii) adoption and implementation of participatory governance programs to engage relevant stakeholders including farmers and fisherfolk, civil society, youth groups, and agriculture professionals.

Following the institutionalization of the NFP, the Congress approved the government's request for budget allocations for 2021 and 2022 to allow the Department of Education and Department of Social Welfare and Development to continue providing children with nutritious food products.

For accurate targeting of RCEF beneficiaries, the government started updating the Registry System for Basic Sectors in Agriculture (RSBSA) covering around 1.956 million rice farmers with sex-disaggregated data.

The government (i) implemented a pilot food voucher program for people affected in the recent Typhoon Odette, and (ii) building on it, initiated a feasibility study to assess the potential for food voucher program to reduce malnutrition for poor pregnant and lactating women and their children under a nationwide nutritional food program as part of the government's zero-hunger agenda.

The government (through DA-ACPC) provided a total of ₱5.97 billion concessional loans to (i) 105,721 smallholder farmers and fisherfolk (SFF), of which 40.0% are female, and 195 agri-fishery micro- and small-sized enterprises (AFMSEs), under the SURE COVID-19 Program to help SFF and MSE mitigate impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic; (ii) 512 SFF, of which 44.0% are female, and 16 AFMSEs, under the Kapital Access for Young Agripreneurs credit program (KAYA); and (iii) 22,207 SFF, of which 52.0% are female, and 175 AFMSEs, under the Agri-Negosyo Loan Program (ANYO) under which an exclusive credit program for agribusiness women (ANYO Agri-Pinay) was established in 2021, thereby enabling women's access to credit.

The government (through the DA) provided smallholder rice farmers with unconditional cash transfers of ₱3.0 billion in the 2020 GAA, ₱2.1 billion in the 2021 GAA, and ₱5.4 billion in the 2021 Unprogrammed Appropriations; and allocated ₱8.9 billion in the 2022 GAA to mitigate the negative immediate impacts of the RTL.

The government (through the NFA Council) reformed the rice buffer stock management by (i) setting an optimal level of rice inventory at 300,000 metric tons for emergency situations and disaster relief operations of the government, and (ii) following the implementing guidelines that lay down the rules, regulations and procedures governing the acquisition, maintenance, and distribution of the government rice buffer stocks.

The government (through the National Economic and Development Authority) adopted and commenced the implementation of the Philippine Water Supply and Sanitation Master Plan 2021─2030 to (i) streamline and rationalize more than 30 water-related bodies, including at least 13 agencies involved in irrigation water governance for effective planning, policy and regulatory development, following the Integrated Water Resources Management principles; (ii) provide direction for identifying key infrastructure investments, which integrates climate resilience; and (iii) incorporate specific measures to improve women's access to water supply and sanitation.

The government continued the operation of RCEF to strengthen the rice sector through mechanization, seeds, extension services, and credit assistance programs with annual allocations of ₱10 billion in 2021 and 2022.

The government developed and commenced the implementation of the national agriculture sector strategy “the National Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization and Industrialization Plan 2021─2030 (NAFMIP)” to transform the sector by increasing financing, raising productivity and income of farmers and fisherfolk, promoting diversification of agriculture subsectors, increasing mechanization, and including strategies to empower women by setting targets to increase women beneficiaries of agri-fishery programs and projects.

The government dismantled a state monopoly for rice and improved food governance by removing the regulatory powers and commercial functions of the National Food Authority (NFA) and transforming it into an emergency buffer stock management agency.

The government enacted the Republic Act 11573 amending (i) the Public Land Act and (ii) the Property Registration Decree to simplify land titling procedures and requirements for agricultural lands by (i) reducing the possession or occupation requirement for the application for AFP from 30 years to 20 years, (ii) extending indefinitely the period for filing of the application for AFP, (iii) setting a maximum AFP application processing period of 120 calendar days, (iv) delegating the authority to issue certification of alienable and disposable agricultural land involving judicial confirmation of imperfect or incomplete title from Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Secretary to DENR regional offices, and (v) removing gender bias in reference to heads of households.

The government established the Rice Farmer Financial Assistance (RFFA) Program and allocated (i) ₱3.0 billion in 2019 GAA to provide unconditional cash transfers to small rice farmers that were affected by low rice farmgate prices, and (ii) ₱3.0 billion in 2020 GAA under the Financial Subsidy to Rice Farmers (FSRF) Program to provide unconditional cash transfers to small farmers also affected by low farmgate prices in areas not covered by the RFFA.

The government facilitated agricultural trade by removing non-tariff barriers and streamlining administrative procedures on the importation of agricultural products and rolling out the government's online trade facilitation portal (TradeNet) with the Department of Agriculture as a key regulatory agency.
The government issued implementing guidelines for four RCEF programs: farm mechanization, seeds development and distribution, extension and training services, and credit assistance.

The government submitted to Congress a proposed legislation on the creation of an apex body for the water resources sector, i.e., the Department of Water Resources, which is intended to address the fragmentation in all water-related plans, policies and program/project implementation, to separate water resource regulation from economic regulation, and to rationalize all water related functions in the government, taking into consideration, among others, gender equality, social inclusion, climate resiliency and disaster risk reduction.

The government through the DA-Agriculture Credit Policy Council (ACPC) (i) established the Expanded Survival and Recovery (SURE) Assistance Program for Rice Farmers (SURE Aid Program) that provided 163,827 small rice farmers (one hectare or below), of which 22% are female, with interest-free loans from ₱2.5 billion credit funds sourced from the 2019 GAA and ACPC loan collections; and (ii) established SURE COVID-19 Program and allocated an additional ₱2.5 billion credit funds sourced from the 2020 GAA and ACPC loan collections to provide interest-free loans for small farmers and fisherfolk (three hectares or below) and AFMSEs affected by COVID-19 pandemic.

The government, through the DA, (i) established 17 Provincial Agricultural and Fishery Extension Centers (PAFEC) and (ii) funded an additional 60 PAFECs to strengthen local government units' agriculture extension services to farmer households with 51.6% active participation by female family members.

The government, through the DPWH, (i) developed FRMMPs for additional eight priority principal river basins, including climate change considerations, and gender analysis and recommendations; and (ii) allocated approximately ₱1.0 billion in the 2022 GAA to commence the implementation of priority measures for six of those eight FRMMPs.

To improve child's nutrition in poor households, the government enacted the Act Institutionalizing a National Feeding Program (NFP) for Undernourished Children in Public Day Care, Kindergarten and Elementary Schools and allocated ₱3.7 billion in 2020 GAA.

To improve rice sector competitiveness under the liberalized trade regime, the government (i) established the Rice Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (RCEF) to support 57 potential rice competitive provinces during 2019-2024 and (ii) allocated ₱10 billion in the GAA 2019 and 2020.

To improve the country's irrigation systems and expand service areas including by addressing climate change impacts and impacts on gender, the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) endorsed the National Irrigation Master Plan 2020-2030 (NIMP).

To reduce flood risk, the government (through the Department of Public Works and Highways) prepared and adopted flood risk management master plans (FRMMPs) for six major river basins, integrating flood protection infrastructure with enhanced flood resilience and response measures in consultation with basin stakeholders, including indigenous people. These master plans also include safeguard impact assessment and gender analysis.

To remove restrictions on agricultural land ownership, the government enacted the Agricultural Free Patent (AFP) Reform Act (2019), making the land titles held by AFP recipient farmers immediately tradeable and bankable, providing them access to capital and credit.

With the redefined functions of the National Food Authority (NFA) under the RTL, the government approved the implementing guidelines on rice buffer stock management to (i) introduce rules and regulations governing the acquisition, maintenance, and distribution of the government rice buffer stocks; and (ii) reform the rice buffer stock management by setting an optimal level of rice inventory at 300,000 metric tons (equivalent to 9 days of national consumption) for emergency situations and disaster relief operations of the government.

Action 2: The government through the DA-Agriculture Credit Policy Council (ACPC) (i) established the Expanded Survival and Recovery (SURE) Assistance Program for Rice Farmers (SURE Aid Program) that provided 163,827 small rice farmers (one hectare or below), of which 22% are female, with interest-free loans from ₱2.5 billion credit funds sourced from the 2019 GAA and ACPC loan collections; and (ii) established SURE COVID-19 Program and allocated an additional ₱2.5 billion credit funds sourced from the 2020 GAA and ACPC loan collections to provide interest-free loans for small farmers and fisherfolk (three hectares or below) and AFMSEs affected by COVID-19 pandemic. Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 3: To improve child's nutrition in poor households, the government enacted the Act Institutionalizing a National Feeding Program (NFP) for Undernourished Children in Public Day Care, Kindergarten and Elementary Schools and allocated ₱3.7 billion in 2020 GAA. Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 1: The government (through the DA) provided smallholder rice farmers with unconditional cash transfers of ₱3.0 billion in the 2020 GAA, ₱2.1 billion in the 2021 GAA, and ₱5.4 billion in the 2021 Unprogrammed Appropriations; and allocated ₱8.9 billion in the 2022 GAA to mitigate the negative immediate impacts of the RTL. Target date: 2022-07-31
